title: Postmortem follow-up: API gateway token-refresh race caused quota miscount and 429 cascade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 a token refresh path in the API gateway exposed a race condition that caused duplicate quota increments for a subset of short-lived tokens. Bursty client retries after token rotation amplified the miscount, causing widespread 429 responses (a '429 cascade') across multiple regions for ~18 minutes. This ticket captures the postmortem actions, owners, and tracking for long-term fixes and monitoring improvements.
root_cause: The gateway's quota enforcement was implemented as two separate operations: (1) store new token metadata and (2) increment per-key usage counter. Under a concurrent token refresh/rotate workload a race allowed the same logical token to be treated as two distinct quota keys for ~30s, resulting in double counting. Additionally, telemetry did not expose token-refresh related quota deltas which delayed detection.
timeline_summary: 02:14 UTC - first anomalous 429s seen in Canary zone; 02:18 UTC - alerts threshold hit across US regions; 02:22 UTC - mitigation: temporarily disabled aggressive client-side retry policy via proxy config; 02:30 UTC - hotfix deployed to gateway that serialized token create + quota increment; 02:40 UTC - 429s subsided; 02:52 UTC - full recovery. Total incident duration ~38 minutes, customer-visible ~18 minutes.
impact_summary: ~1.5M requests affected, peaking at 18% of total traffic for the primary API route. 12 enterprise customers saw increased error rates; 3 customers reported functional impact to background jobs. No data loss or exfiltration. Major impact to latency and error-rate dashboards; SLA credits being evaluated for two customers.
immediate_mitigation: Temporary mitigation applied: serialized path in gateway for token refresh using an in-process lock + short TTL on duplicate-key suppression. Also lowered default client retry multiplier at edge via CDN config to reduce amplification. Enabled emergency dashboard with token-refresh vs quota-delta graph.
long_term_actions: ENG-7680: Replace two-step quota increment with atomic Redis Lua script that enforces idempotency (owner: Marco Li, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-7691: Add idempotency-key support for token refresh RPCs and persist idemp key for 60s (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-7702: Add load-test scenario simulating high token-rotation churn in k6 harness and include in CI (owner: Daniel Kim, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-7727: Extend telemetry: emit token-refresh metric, quota-delta-by-reason and per-region backpressure counters (owner: Maria Gomez, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-7745: Update runbook: include token-rotation incident checklist and automatic mitigation playbook (owner: Marco Li, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-7758: Add circuit-breaker in gateway to backoff clients when quota delta spike is detected (owner: Chloe Zhang, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-7762: Post-incident customer outreach & SLA decision coordination with CS (owner: Riya Shah, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-7770: Backport atomic quota fix to dedicated/private runtime branches and plan canary rollout (owner: Marco Li, due: 2026-03-30)
accepted_risk_or_tradeoffs: Atomic Redis Lua script adds a small P99 latency increase (~1-2ms) on quota path but eliminates double-count risk. We accept higher percentile cost in exchange for correctness; compensating optimization will focus on batching counters for low-latency clients.
blockers: Awaiting ops approval for account-level rollout policy (security/ops) - ticket OPS-1145
Coordination with dedicated/private runtime teams for backporting windows
monitoring_changes: alerting/420-quota-spike-policy (lowered initial threshold and added token-refresh anomaly filter)
retro_notes: Decision: implement atomic quota increments via Redis Lua (favored for simplicity and auditability)
We will prioritize telemetry & testing before enabling aggressive batching/quantization changes across customers
Assign a quarterly review to validate the token-refresh regression suite in load testing
